feed.title: Piracy & FMHY — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Anna's Archive
entry.summary: A search engine that unifies shadow libraries (Library Genesis, Sci-Hub, Z-Library) in one interface.

entry.title: archive.today
entry.summary: An archiver that freezes a page exactly as it is and produces a permanent snapshot.

entry.title: Awesome Piracy
entry.summary: The source list most of this field’s links come from; it gathers media, games, books and tools by category. Unlike FMHY it is a GitHub repository open to contribution.

entry.title: Bazarr
entry.summary: A companion that automatically finds and downloads subtitles for your Sonarr/Radarr library. Unlike hunting subtitles by hand it rules the language and quality and keeps filling gaps.

entry.title: CORE
entry.summary: The largest aggregator gathering the world's open-access research papers in one place.

entry.title: DOAB — Directory of Open Access Books
entry.summary: A directory of peer-reviewed open-access academic books.

entry.title: DOAJ — Directory of Open Access Journals
entry.summary: A vetted directory of peer-reviewed open-access journals — legal and free.

entry.title: FMHY
entry.summary: “Free Media Heck Yeah” — the largest index of free media, tools and resources. Unlike individual sites it gathers them category by category, with safety notes, and keeps them current.

entry.title: Getting Into Private Trackers
entry.summary: A community guide to how private torrent trackers work and how to get in. Unlike rumour it explains the ratio, invite and rules systems step by step.

entry.title: Internet Archive
entry.summary: A vast digital archive preserving the web, books, audio and video — home of the Wayback Machine.

entry.title: IPFS
entry.summary: A decentralised file system that addresses content by its hash, not its location. Unlike classic hosting the same file can come from many nodes, resistant to censorship.

entry.title: Jellyfin
entry.summary: A fully open-source, free counterpart to Plex; no feature behind a paywall. Unlike Plex it is not tied to a central account — everything stays on your server.

entry.title: Kodi
entry.summary: Open-source media-centre software gathering local and network media in one interface. Unlike the server model it runs directly on the device and extends through add-ons.

entry.title: Library Genesis
entry.summary: A widely used shadow library hosting books and academic articles.

entry.title: LibreTexts
entry.summary: A free platform compiling university-level open textbooks subject by subject.

entry.title: Open Library
entry.summary: Internet Archive's open catalogue aiming for a page per book, lending many of them.

entry.title: Overseerr
entry.summary: A request interface that takes the household’s film/series requests and passes them to the *arr tools. Unlike direct server access it lets a non-technical user request with a button.

entry.title: Perma.cc
entry.summary: Creates permanent archived copies of cited links to stop link rot; library-backed.

entry.title: Plex
entry.summary: A server that organises your own media library and streams it to any device. Unlike folder sharing it auto-fetches posters, summaries and subtitles and builds a Netflix-like interface.

entry.title: Project Gutenberg
entry.summary: The oldest digital library, offering 70,000+ public-domain classics for free.

entry.title: Prowlarr
entry.summary: A bridge that manages torrent and Usenet indexers in one place and connects them to the *arr tools. Unlike configuring each tool separately it centralises the indexer list.

entry.title: qBittorrent
entry.summary: An ad-free, open-source BitTorrent client with built-in search and sequential streaming. Unlike closed clients it carries no bundled software or ads.

entry.title: r/Piracy Megathread
entry.summary: A resource index maintained by the r/Piracy community, organised by area. Unlike random search it is community-vetted, with dead and trap links weeded out.

entry.title: r/Usenet Wiki
entry.summary: A community guide to getting started with Usenet and choosing providers and indexers. Unlike ad sites it is comparative, neutral and experience-based.

entry.title: Radarr
entry.summary: The film counterpart to Sonarr — it watches your wishlist and downloads automatically when a suitable release appears. Unlike searching one by one it picks the best source by quality profile.

entry.title: SABnzbd
entry.summary: An open-source client that automates Usenet downloads — including verification, repair and extraction. Unlike manual downloading it takes an NZB and completes the whole chain itself.

entry.title: Sci-Hub
entry.summary: A controversial repository providing access to paywalled academic papers.

entry.title: Sonarr
entry.summary: A tool that watches TV series and automatically fetches and organises new episodes via a downloader. Unlike manual tracking it puts quality, naming and archiving under rules.

entry.title: Standard Ebooks
entry.summary: A volunteer project that carefully typesets and formats public-domain books, free.

entry.title: Tautulli
entry.summary: A tool that monitors and reports plays and users on your Plex server. Unlike Plex’s own stats it offers detailed history, notifications and charts.

entry.title: Transmission
entry.summary: A lightweight, open-source BitTorrent client that can run headless on a server. Unlike desktop clients it uses few resources and suits remote management.

entry.title: Unpaywall
entry.summary: A tool and browser extension that finds legal open-access copies of paywalled papers.

entry.title: AudiobookBay
entry.summary: A community site sharing audiobooks via torrents and direct links. Unlike book-focused archives it deals only in audiobooks.

entry.title: FreeBookSpot
entry.summary: A categorised directory of direct-download ebooks. Unlike a single archive such as Anna's Archive/LibGen, it is a catalogue linking out to external hosts.

entry.title: ManyBooks
entry.summary: A library offering public-domain and indie-author ebooks for free in many formats (EPUB, PDF, Kindle).

entry.title: Online Library of Liberty
entry.summary: Liberty Fund's open library offering classic works on liberty, economics and political philosophy (Locke, Smith, Mill…) for free. Unlike shadow libraries everything here is public-domain or openly licensed and carefully typeset.

entry.title: Torrent-Finder
entry.summary: A meta-search engine that queries dozens of torrent sites at once from one interface — a search layer over many trackers, not a single tracker.
